mainTopic: בן ננס's rule that the last of two conflicting phrases decides: whether the חכמים disagree, and what שמואל holds.
overview: The משנה ends with בן ננס's rule: when a seller says two conflicting phrases, the last phrase cancels the first. רב says that בן ננס's colleagues disagree with him. The גמרא asks what this adds, since a משנה about renting a bathhouse in a leap year already shows that the חכמים split the doubtful money. It answers that in the bathhouse case the second phrase might only have explained how to pay, while in our משנה the seller clearly changed his mind. Next, שמואל says that following the last phrase is בן ננס's view, and the חכמים follow the phrase that gives the least. The גמרא points to a grain-sale ruling of רב and שמואל that follows the last phrase, so it rereads שמואל as agreeing with בן ננס. Then it challenges that reading from שמואל's own explanation of the bathhouse case, where he decides by who holds the property or the money, not by the last phrase. The answer to this clash comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The last words cancel the first words, according to בן ננס
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its case: if the seller said 'more or less' and then 'measured with a rope,' the last phrase, 'measured with a rope,' cancels 'more or less.' This is the view of בן ננס.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Measured with a rope' cancels 'more or less.' These are the words of בן ננס.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It gives בן ננס's rule that when a seller says two conflicting things, his last words are the ones that count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'More or less' allows a small difference in the size of the field. 'Measured with a rope' means the size must be exact. When both are said, בן ננס follows whichever phrase came last, so here the sale must be exact.

keyTerms.meaning: cancels, makes void
measured with a rope, an exact measurement
whether less or more, a rough amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that we follow the last words, is the subject of the whole גמרא that comes next.

phrases.english: 'Measured with a rope' cancels
phrases.notes: Here the seller said 'more or less' first and 'measured with a rope' second, so the second phrase wins.

phrases.english: 'more or less';
these are the words of ben Nanas.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּטֵּל מִדָּה בְּחֶבֶל הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר דִּבְרֵי בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן ננס, when a seller says two conflicting phrases, the last phrase decides.

steps.title: רב says בן ננס's colleagues disagree with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל quotes רב: the other חכמים disagree with בן ננס.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אבא בר ממל said in the name of רב: בן ננס's colleagues disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב's statement that the other חכמים do not agree with בן ננס's rule about following the last words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is telling us that the rule 'the last words decide' is not accepted by everyone. That raises a question: did we not already know this? The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion of the משנה
they disagree
his colleagues, the other חכמים

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Abba bar Memel says
Rav says:
His colleagues disagree with him,
with ben Nanas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל אָמַר רַב חוֹלְקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on בן ננס's rule from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים disagree with בן ננס and do not automatically follow the last phrase.

steps.title: We already know this from the bathhouse case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב adds. A משנה already tells of a man who rented a bathhouse for 'twelve gold coins a year, one gold dinar a month.' When a leap-year month was added, the חכמים ruled that the two sides split that month. So they clearly do not just follow the last words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב teaching us? We already learned it: There was a case in ציפורי of a man who rented a bathhouse from his fellow for twelve gold coins a year, one gold dinar a month. The case came before רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יוסי, and they said: They should split the extra leap-year month!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. It says his statement is not new, because a משנה about renting a bathhouse already shows that the חכמים disagree with בן ננס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a leap year, 'twelve a year' means the 13th month is free. 'A dinar a month' means it costs a dinar. If the חכמים followed the last words, as בן ננס does, the renter would pay the full dinar. Instead they had the two sides split it, which shows they treat the conflict as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
bathhouse
gold coins
the extra month added in a leap year
they should split it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים in the bathhouse case followed the first words either. They followed neither phrase. They treated it as a doubt and had both sides split the money.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned it:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא מציעא (102a).

phrases.english: There was an incident in Tzippori,
with one who rented a bathhouse from his fellow
for twelve gold coins a year —
a gold dinar per month;

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: and the case came before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
and before Rabbi Yosei,
and they said:
They should split the extra leap-year month!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the חכמים disagree with בן ננס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bathhouse משנה already shows that the חכמים split the money instead of following the last phrase. So רב's statement adds nothing new.

steps.title: The bathhouse case was unclear; our case is a clear change of mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: from the bathhouse case alone, we might think the חכמים split the money only because the second phrase could have been an explanation of how to pay. In our משנה, the second phrase clearly takes back the first, so we might think the חכמים agree with בן ננס. רב teaches that they disagree even here.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that case, I would have said: there, it could be that he took back his words, and it could be that he was just explaining them. But here, where he certainly took back his words, I might say they agree. So רב teaches us that they disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It shows that the bathhouse case is weaker than our case, so רב's statement does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the bathhouse case, 'a dinar a month' might just mean 'pay monthly' and not change the price, so there was a real doubt. In our משנה, 'more or less' and 'measured with a rope' cannot both be true, so the seller clearly changed his mind. רב teaches that even then, the חכמים do not automatically follow the last words.

keyTerms.meaning: if we only had it from there
I would have thought
he is taking back his words
he is just explaining his words
certainly

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים disagree with בן ננס even when the second phrase clearly takes back the first. They do not automatically follow the last words. The bathhouse case alone could not teach this, because there the second phrase might only have been an explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the difference between a doubt about what someone meant and a clear change of mind. It also shows that the חכמים' view applies in both cases.

phrases.english: If we only had it from there,
I would have said:
it is there

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מִיהְדָּר קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that one can say he is taking back his words,
and one can say he is just explaining them.
phrases.notes: 'Explaining' means 'a dinar a month' only told him to pay monthly. It wasn't a new price.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּוַדַּאי קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: But here, where he certainly takes back his words,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה. 'More or less' and 'measured with a rope' can't both be true.

phrases.english: I might say they do not disagree;
so he teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by showing how the bathhouse case differs from ours.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a doubtful second phrase versus a clear change of mind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים split the money only when the second phrase might just be an explanation. When the seller clearly changed his mind, they would agree with בן ננס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים disagree with בן ננס even when the seller clearly changed his mind, so רב's statement teaches something new.

steps.title: שמואל says: this is בן ננס, but the חכמים follow the weaker phrase
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the rule in our משנה is the view of בן ננס. The חכמים say to follow the phrase that gives the buyer the least.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of בן ננס. But the חכמים say: follow the phrase that gives the least.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report, this time from שמואל, says that 'the last phrase wins' is only בן ננס's view. It also tells us what the חכמים actually hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב in step 2 only said the חכמים disagree. שמואל adds their rule: when two phrases clash, the buyer gets only what the smaller phrase gives him. The one who wants to take something from the other must prove his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the view of'. It names who said a ruling.
Follow, or go by
The phrase that gives the least

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is the view of ben Nanas,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that the last phrase, 'measured with a rope,' wins.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:
Follow the phrase that gives the least.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel report to רב's statement in step 2. It also spells out what the חכמים hold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following the last phrase is בן ננס's view. The חכמים follow the phrase that gives the least.

steps.title: Does שמואל disagree with בן ננס? A grain sale case says he agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'this is בן ננס' as meaning שמואל disagrees. But רב and שמואל ruled about grain sold 'a כור for thirty, a סאה for a סלע', and there the last phrase wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does 'this is בן ננס' mean שמואל does not hold that way? But רב and שמואל both said: 'I sell you a כור for thirty': the seller can back out even at the last סאה. 'I sell you a כור for thirty, a סאה for a סלע': the buyer owns each סאה as it is measured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that שמואל disagrees with בן ננס. It brings a ruling of רב and שמואל that seems to follow the last phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller only says 'a כור,' the sale is one whole unit, so he can back out until all of it is given. If he adds 'a סאה for a סלע,' that last phrase makes each סאה a separate sale. The later words control the deal, which is exactly בן ננס's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not hold this way?
A large measure of grain, equal to thirty סאה
A measure of grain, one thirtieth of a כור
A silver coin
To back out of the deal
He acquires each part, one at a time

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'זו' (this) can be read two ways: 'this is only בן ננס, not me,' or 'this is בן ננס, and I agree.' The whole back-and-forth in steps 6 and 7 is about which reading is right.

phrases.english: 'This' is ben Nanas's view, and he does not hold that way?!
But Rav and Shmuel both say:
'I am selling you a kor for thirty' –
he can back out
even at the last se'a.

phrases.aramaic: ״כּוֹר בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים – סְאָה בְּסֶלַע אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ –
phrases.english: 'I am selling you a kor for thirty, a se'a for a sela' –
he acquires each one as it comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זוֹ״ – וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?! וְהָא רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading that in step 5 שמואל disagrees with בן ננס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of שמואל's 'זו' as 'only בן ננס, not me'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל ruled in the grain case that the later phrase 'a סאה for a סלע' controls. That matches בן ננס, so שמואל cannot disagree with him.

steps.title: Reread it: 'this is בן ננס, and שמואל agrees'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how it reads שמואל: 'this is בן ננס's view, and I hold like him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'this' is בן ננס's view, and שמואל agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading שמואל's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זו דברי בן ננס' now just names the source of the rule and does not reject it. This fits the grain ruling, where שמואל follows the last phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in a new explanation.
And he does hold this way

phrases.english: Rather, 'this' is ben Nanas's view, and he does hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by changing how שמואל's statement is read.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זו דברי בן ננס' meant שמואל rejects בן ננס.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל names בן ננס as the source and agrees with him.

steps.title: But שמואל's bathhouse ruling shows he does not follow the last words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really agrees with בן ננס. He explained that in the bathhouse case the חכמים split the extra month only when the owner came mid-month. At the start of the month all of it goes to the owner, and at the end all of it goes to the renter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does שמואל really hold this way? But שמואל said: we are dealing with a case where the owner came to collect in the middle of the month. If he came at the start of the month, it all goes to the owner. If he came at the end of the month, it all goes to the renter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against the answer in step 7. It uses שמואל's own explanation of the bathhouse case from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the last phrase won, 'one dinar a month' would always decide the matter, and the renter would always pay for the extra month. Instead, שמואל treats it as a doubt. The question is who holds the disputed time or money: the owner holds the bathhouse at the start of the month, and the renter holds the money at the end. So שמואל does not follow the last phrase, which goes against step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold this way?
We are dealing with this case
The owner who rents out the property
The renter

phrases.english: And does he really hold that way?!
But didn't Shmuel say:
phrases.notes: שמואל is explaining the bathhouse משנה from step 3, where the חכמים split the leap-year month.

phrases.english: we are dealing with a case where he came in the middle of the month;
phrases.notes: 'He came' means the owner came to collect the rent.

phrases.english: but if he came at the beginning of the month –
all of it goes to the owner.
If he came at the end of the month –
all of it goes to the renter!

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clash between two rulings of שמואל: the grain sale and the bathhouse. The גמרא will have to make them fit together.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 7 that שמואל agrees with בן ננס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that שמואל holds like בן ננס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the bathhouse case, שמואל decides by who holds the property or the money, not by the last phrase. So he does not follow בן ננס's rule.
